title: The Long-lost Son, with Streaming Eyes
description: The Long-lost Son, with Streaming Eyes in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 324 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Prodigal's Return”, where the book credits them to the Village Hymns.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The long lost son, with stream-ing eyes, From fol-ly just a-wake, Re-views his wan-derings with sur-prise; His heart be-gins to break.

lines: The long-lost son, with streaming eyes,
"I starve," he cries, "nor can I bear
While servants of my Father share
Unworthy to be called a son,
Far off the Father saw him move,
And quickly ran with arms of love,
O, let thy boundless mercy shine
Correct my passions, mend my heart,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
